chunks.text: A message threatening immediate account deactivation may be phishing. Pause before following its verification link and independently check the request with your bank.
Treat unexpected KYC calls asking you to install remote-access software or disclose card details with caution. Verify the request with the bank through an independently obtained official contact.

Do not transfer money under pressure from a caller claiming to be police or another authority. Verify the claim directly with your local police station. Report cyber fraud promptly through cybercrime.gov.in or 1930.

Be cautious of trading apps promising high returns with little risk. Check that the broker is SEBI-registered and use the registered broker’s official app or website instead of transferring funds to personal accounts.
Do not disclose an OTP to a caller or someone claiming to be bank support. SBI states that it does not ask customers for OTPs.
Keep passwords private and use a different strong password for each account. Enable multi-factor authentication where available.
Phishing messages imitate trusted organisations to collect personal or financial information. Check the destination carefully and pause before acting on urgent links asking for sensitive details.

Do not pay an unsolicited contact who promises to recover money lost to a scam for an upfront fee. Independently verify organisations that contact you, and do not disclose financial credentials to obtain a refund.
Do not install a third-party application at the request of someone claiming to represent SBI. A request to install remote-control software can expose your device and banking information.
Do not disclose an OTP or UPI PIN to receive money. If a caller asks for payment credentials, use the institution’s independently verified customer-care channel.
